summary.intent: Resolve review feedback on michi PRs: fix a finding on change #53 (pushed to #141) and decide whether to keep the cargo-semver-checks CI job added in #140.
summary.outcome: Error-cause byte charging was fixed and pushed to #141 (58363219) with a regression test and passing checks. The user decided changesets are intentional, so the semver CI job, scripts/check-semver.sh and the related recipe were removed from #140, then committed and pushed.

repo: michi uses Callisto changesets to declare version bumps; the user treats them as deliberate, so CI that second-guesses the bump level is unwanted.
Before 1.0, almost every michi release is a minor bump, which may break the API. The semver check only mattered for breaking changes hidden in patch releases (e.g. 0.7.1).
There is a separate check-api check that verifies docs change when public API changes; it is unrelated to the semver check and was kept.
Error causes in the output-size accounting are charged like hints (text + 1 byte), not text + 24, so a full 10,000-cause report fits a fresh builder.
There are 14 output-bound tests guarding the output-size guarantee.
The test suite has about 1,191 non-scaling Rust tests, 183 Node tests and 18 scaling tests. `just check` is the main local gate.
Branch protection is implemented via repository rulesets, so removing a CI job requires checking whether it is a required check.

code.finding: Removed along with the semver CI job and its just recipe. It was a shell script calling `callisto status` to get the pending bump for cargo-semver-checks.

workflow: Before removing a CI job, check whether branch protection or rulesets require it, and grep docs for references.
Scaling tests can fail spuriously under heavy machine load (load average 155) and should be rerun alone to confirm.
Validate a regression test by reverting the fix and confirming it fails with the original error.

friction: High machine load (load average 155) caused the 18 scaling tests to fail in the full run, needing isolated reruns.
Spent effort recommending and explaining a semver check that the user had already decided against on principle.
open_items: Possibly re-add semver checking before 1.0 if patch releases become more common (not pursued, since the user rejected it).
The npm package was never covered by semver checking.
